Choosing between Shopify and Shopify Plus may not seem as easy as it can be, because even some experts get confused when it comes to Shopify Plus vs Shopify. But to be honest, it all comes down to one question: does your business need enterprise-level tools, or does standard Shopify already cover you?

So, let’s have a direct, feature-by-feature Shopify Plus comparison that can easily help us decide.

Feature Standard Shopify Shopify Plus
Starting price 39–399/month ~$2,300/month
Checkout customization Limited, app-based Full control via Checkout Extensibility
B2B features Core B2B on all plans (since April 2026) Unlimited catalogs, per-buyer catalog assignment, deposits, partial payments
Automation Basic, mostly manual or app-based Shopify Flow, Launchpad for automated sales events
API limits Standard rate limits Significantly higher API call limits
Staff accounts Limited by plan Unlimited
Expansion stores Not included Up to 9 included
POS Pro $89/month per location Included free for all locations
Support Standard support Dedicated Merchant Success Manager

Pricing

Pricing

Standard Shopify will cost you $39 to $399 a month, depending on the plan. Shopify Plus starts at around $2,300 a month, with revenue-based pricing at higher volumes. That’s a big jump, but Plus also offers lower transaction fees, which start to offset the cost as sales grow.

Checkout

This is one of the clearest differences. Standard Shopify offers a fixed, app-dependent checkout. Shopify Plus gives full checkout customization through Checkout Extensibility, letting you add custom fields, upsells, and trust elements exactly where you want them. If your checkout is holding back conversions, this alone can justify the upgrade.

B2B

As of April 2026, core B2B tools, like company accounts and payment terms, are available on every Shopify plan. This is a real shift. But Plus still leads for serious B2B operations. It removes catalog limits, lets you assign catalogs directly to specific buyers, and adds deposit and partial-payment options standard plans don’t have.

Automation

Standard Shopify handles basic tasks well but leans on apps for anything more complex. Shopify Plus features includes Shopify Flow for building custom, code-free workflows, plus Launchpad, which automates entire sales events from start to finish, including price changes, theme updates, and reverting everything once the sale ends.

APIs and Integrations

If your business relies on multiple integrations, this matters. Standard Shopify API limits can throttle complex setups. Plus offers significantly higher limits, which matter most for businesses running several connected systems, like ERP, CRM, or custom apps.

Scalability

Standard Shopify works well for predictable, steady traffic. Plus is built for scale. It handles high-traffic events, like flash sales, without slowing down and gives businesses more staff accounts and backend flexibility as they grow.

International Commerce

Selling in multiple countries? Plus includes up to nine expansion stores, each with its own currency, storefront, and product selection. Standard Shopify can sell internationally too, but without the same level of built-in multi-store management.

Recommendations by Business Type

  • New or small stores: Standard Shopify is the right call. It’s affordable, capable, and won’t overwhelm a small team.
  • Growing DTC brands ($1M+ revenue): Start evaluating Plus, especially if checkout conversion or automation needs are becoming a bottleneck.
  • B2B and wholesale-heavy businesses: Plus is usually worth it once you need unlimited catalogs or buyer-specific pricing beyond what standard plans offer.
  • Multi-country or multi-brand businesses: Plus’s expansion stores make managing several storefronts far easier.
  • Businesses with complex integrations: If API limits are throttling your systems, Plus removes that ceiling.

The Bottom Line

Standard Shopify covers most small and mid-sized stores well, especially now that core B2B tools are no longer Plus-exclusive. Shopify Plus earns its price when your business needs deep checkout control, heavy automation, multiple storefronts, or B2B operations at scale.

Not sure which side of that line your business falls on? Talk to a Shopify Plus development partner to map your specific needs against the real feature differences, not just the price tag.
